title: Childhood Memories
subtitle: Talk about the past with the imparfait

lessons.title: Quand j'étais petit
lessons.description: Learn to form the imparfait and describe what life was like when you were a child.

blocks.heading: A tense for how things were
blocks.body: The imparfait is the past tense French uses for descriptions, habits and background — what things WERE like, what people USED TO do. It does not tell one single completed event; it paints the scene. It often translates as "used to" or "was/were ...-ing".

examples.french: Quand j'étais petit, j'habitais à Lyon.
examples.english: When I was little, I lived in Lyon.

examples.french: Je jouais dans le jardin tous les jours.
examples.english: I used to play in the garden every day.

examples.french: Ma grand-mère racontait des histoires.
examples.english: My grandmother used to tell stories.

examples.french: Nous regardions des dessins animés le samedi.
examples.english: We used to watch cartoons on Saturdays.

examples.french: Il faisait toujours beau en été.
examples.english: The weather was always nice in summer.

blocks.tip: Time words like "tous les jours", "souvent", "toujours" and "à l'époque" are strong signals for the imparfait.

blocks.heading: How to form it
blocks.body: Take the "nous" form of the present tense, drop -ons, and add the imparfait endings: -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient. Example: nous jouons → jou- → je jouais. The only irregular stem in the whole language is être → ét-.

examples.french: jouer → nous jouons → je jouais
examples.english: to play → we play → I used to play

examples.french: finir → nous finissons → tu finissais
examples.english: to finish → we finish → you used to finish

examples.french: faire → nous faisons → il faisait
examples.english: to do → we do → he used to do

examples.french: avoir → nous avons → nous avions
examples.english: to have → we have → we used to have

examples.french: être → ét- → vous étiez
examples.english: to be → you were

examples.french: aller → nous allons → elles allaient
examples.english: to go → they used to go

blocks.tip: The endings -ais, -ait and -aient all sound the same: "eh". Only -ions and -iez sound different.

blocks.heading: Talking about childhood
blocks.body: French speakers introduce childhood memories with set phrases: "quand j'étais petit(e)" (when I was little), "à l'époque" (back then), "autrefois" (in the old days). A girl or woman says "petite", a boy or man says "petit".

blocks.heading: The imparfait, step by step
blocks.body: One rule covers almost every verb: present-tense "nous" form minus -ons, plus the endings -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient. Watch the spelling of -ger and -cer verbs: manger → je mangeais (extra e), commencer → je commençais (ç) before endings starting with a.

examples.french: j'habitais, tu habitais, il habitait
examples.english: I / you / he used to live

examples.french: nous habitions, vous habitiez, elles habitaient
examples.english: we / you / they used to live

examples.french: je mangeais du pain au chocolat
examples.english: I used to eat pain au chocolat
examples.note: extra e keeps the soft g sound

examples.french: on commençait l'école à huit heures
examples.english: school started at eight
examples.note: ç keeps the soft c sound

examples.french: c'était, il y avait, il faisait
examples.english: it was, there was/were, the weather was
examples.note: three imparfait forms you will use constantly

blocks.tip: Memorize "c'était" and "il y avait" as chunks — they open almost every memory: "C'était super, il y avait beaucoup d'enfants."

blocks.heading: When to use it
blocks.body: Use the imparfait for: 1) repeated habits (je jouais tous les jours), 2) descriptions of people, places and weather (il faisait froid, elle était petite), 3) feelings and states (j'avais peur, je voulais un chien). For one completed event, French uses the passé composé instead — you will combine the two in lesson 3.

examples.french: Tous les étés, nous allions à la mer.
examples.english: Every summer, we went to the seaside.

examples.french: La maison était grande et blanche.

examples.french: J'avais sept ans.
examples.english: I was seven years old.
examples.note: state — age always takes the imparfait

examples.french: Mes parents travaillaient beaucoup.
examples.english: My parents worked a lot.

lessons.title: Avant et maintenant
lessons.description: Compare the past and the present: imparfait vs présent, and comparisons with plus, moins and aussi.

blocks.heading: Before and now
blocks.body: To contrast the past with the present, French pairs the imparfait with the present tense, often introduced by "avant" (before) and "maintenant" (now). The tense change alone tells the listener which period you mean.

examples.french: Avant, j'habitais à la campagne. Maintenant, j'habite en ville.
examples.english: Before, I lived in the countryside. Now, I live in the city.

examples.french: Avant, on écrivait des lettres. Maintenant, on envoie des messages.
examples.english: Before, people wrote letters. Now, people send messages.

examples.french: Avant, je regardais des dessins animés. Maintenant, je regarde les infos.
examples.english: Before, I watched cartoons. Now, I watch the news.

examples.french: Avant, la rue était calme. Maintenant, elle est très bruyante.
examples.english: Before, the street was quiet. Now, it is very noisy.

examples.french: Avant, je n'avais pas de portable.
examples.english: Before, I didn't have a cell phone.

blocks.tip: In negative imparfait sentences, ne...pas wraps around the verb, just like in the present: "je ne jouais pas".

blocks.heading: Comparing with plus, moins, aussi
blocks.body: To compare, put "plus" (more), "moins" (less) or "aussi" (as) before an adjective or adverb, and "que" after it: plus calme que (calmer than), moins cher que (less expensive than), aussi grand que (as tall as).

examples.french: La vie était plus simple qu'aujourd'hui.
examples.english: Life was simpler than today.

examples.french: Mon quartier est moins calme qu'avant.
examples.english: My neighborhood is less quiet than before.

examples.french: Je suis aussi occupé que mes parents.
examples.english: I am as busy as my parents.

examples.french: Les gens sortaient plus souvent.
examples.english: People used to go out more often.

examples.french: Avec le métro, c'est plus pratique.
examples.english: With the metro, it's more convenient.

blocks.tip: "Que" becomes "qu'" before a vowel: plus calme qu'avant.

blocks.heading: Better and worse: the irregulars
blocks.body: Two comparisons are irregular. "Bon" (good) becomes "meilleur" (better) — never "plus bon". "Bien" (well) becomes "mieux" (better, adverb). "Mauvais" can become "pire" (worse). Use "autant de + noun" for "as much/many".

examples.english: Bread was better in the old days.

examples.french: Je dors mieux maintenant.
examples.english: I sleep better now.

examples.english: Traffic is worse than before.

blocks.heading: Imparfait vs présent
blocks.body: The contrast "avant + imparfait / maintenant + présent" is one of the most useful patterns at A2. Keep the two tenses clearly separated: everything in the "avant" part goes in the imparfait, everything in the "maintenant" part stays in the present.

blocks.tip: After a negative, "de" replaces un/une/des: je n'avais pas DE portable.

passages.title: La vie a changé
passages.french:
Ma grand-mère dit toujours que la vie a beaucoup changé.
Quand elle était jeune, il n'y avait pas d'Internet et très peu de familles avaient la télévision.
Les gens écrivaient des lettres et attendaient la réponse pendant des semaines.
Maintenant, on envoie un message et la réponse arrive en dix secondes.
Avant, elle faisait ses courses au marché du village.
Aujourd'hui, elle commande parfois sur Internet, mais elle préfère encore le marché.
« C'était plus lent, mais on prenait le temps de parler », dit-elle.
Moi, je pense que la vie moderne est plus pratique, mais peut-être moins calme.
passages.english:

Today, she sometimes orders on the Internet, but she still prefers the market.
"It was slower, but people took the time to talk," she says.
Me, I think modern life is more convenient, but maybe less calm.

lessons.title: Raconter un souvenir
lessons.description: Tell a story from your past by combining the imparfait (background) with the passé composé (events).

blocks.heading: Two tenses, one story
blocks.body: A French story in the past uses both tenses together. The imparfait sets the scene: weather, feelings, what was going on. The passé composé tells the events: what happened, one action after another. Think of a play: the imparfait is the scenery, the passé composé is the actors moving.

examples.french: Il faisait beau. Soudain, il a commencé à pleuvoir.
examples.english: The weather was nice. Suddenly, it started to rain.

examples.french: Je jouais dans le jardin quand je suis tombé.
examples.english: I was playing in the garden when I fell.

examples.french: Nous étions à la plage et nous avons vu un dauphin.
examples.english: We were at the beach and we saw a dolphin.

examples.french: Elle avait cinq ans quand elle a appris à nager.
examples.english: She was five when she learned to swim.

examples.french: J'avais peur, alors j'ai appelé mon père.
examples.english: I was scared, so I called my dad.

blocks.tip: "J'étais en train de + infinitive" stresses an ongoing action: "J'étais en train de dessiner quand tu as téléphoné."

blocks.heading: Words that move the story forward
blocks.body: Storytelling connectors make your memory easy to follow: d'abord (first), puis (then), ensuite (next), soudain / tout à coup (suddenly), enfin (finally), le lendemain (the next day). They usually introduce passé composé events.

examples.french: D'abord, nous avons pris le train.
examples.english: First, we took the train.

examples.french: Puis nous sommes arrivés à la mer.
examples.english: Then we arrived at the seaside.

examples.french: Tout à coup, l'orage a éclaté.
examples.english: All of a sudden, the storm broke.

examples.french: Enfin, nous avons retrouvé notre chien.
examples.english: Finally, we found our dog again.

examples.french: Le lendemain, tout était calme.
examples.english: The next day, everything was calm.

blocks.heading: A memory in action
blocks.body: Watch how a real anecdote mixes the two tenses. Background and feelings take the imparfait; the chain of events takes the passé composé.

examples.french: C'était l'été, j'avais huit ans.
examples.english: It was summer, I was eight.

examples.french: Je faisais du vélo avec mon copain Théo.
examples.english: I was riding my bike with my friend Théo.

examples.french: Soudain, je suis tombé et je me suis cassé le bras.
examples.english: Suddenly, I fell and broke my arm.

examples.french: Ma mère m'a emmené à l'hôpital.
examples.english: My mom took me to the hospital.

examples.french: Heureusement, ce n'était pas grave.
examples.english: Fortunately, it wasn't serious.

blocks.tip: Ask yourself: is this sentence the scenery or an event? Scenery → imparfait. Event → passé composé.

blocks.heading: Choosing the right tense
blocks.body: Ask two questions. 1) Is it background (description, feeling, ongoing action)? → imparfait. 2) Is it a specific completed event that moves the story forward? → passé composé. "Quand" often links them: imparfait situation + passé composé interruption.

examples.french: Je dormais quand le téléphone a sonné.
examples.english: I was sleeping when the phone rang.

examples.french: Il pleuvait, alors nous sommes restés à la maison.
examples.english: It was raining, so we stayed home.

examples.french: Elle regardait la télé quand ses copines sont arrivées.
examples.english: She was watching TV when her friends arrived.

examples.french: Comme j'avais peur, j'ai fermé la porte.
examples.english: As I was scared, I closed the door.

blocks.tip: The interrupted action (was ...-ing) is imparfait; the interruption (rang, arrived) is passé composé.

blocks.heading: Agreement reminders in stories
blocks.body: With être-verbs in the passé composé, the past participle agrees with the subject: elle est tombée, nous sommes partis. With reflexive verbs, agreement usually happens too — but NOT when a body part follows: elle s'est cassé la jambe (no extra -e).

passages.title: Un souvenir inoubliable
passages.french:
Quand j'avais neuf ans, nous passions toujours l'été chez mes grands-parents, près de la forêt.
Un après-midi, je jouais à cache-cache avec mon cousin Hugo.
Je cherchais une bonne cachette, alors je suis entré dans la forêt.
Au début, ce n'était pas grave, mais après une heure, je ne reconnaissais plus le chemin.
J'avais très peur et j'ai crié le nom de mon cousin.
Soudain, j'ai entendu la voix de mon grand-père : il me cherchait avec le chien.
J'ai couru vers lui et il m'a pris dans ses bras.
Le lendemain, toute la famille riait de mon aventure.
Maintenant, c'est un souvenir inoubliable — mais ce jour-là, je ne riais pas du tout !
passages.english:
When I was nine, we always spent the summer at my grandparents' house, near the forest.
One afternoon, I was playing hide-and-seek with my cousin Hugo.
I was looking for a good hiding place, so I went into the forest.
At first, it wasn't serious, but after an hour, I no longer recognized the path.
I was very scared and I shouted my cousin's name.
Suddenly, I heard my grandfather's voice: he was looking for me with the dog.
I ran to him and he took me in his arms.
The next day, the whole family was laughing about my adventure.
Now, it's an unforgettable memory — but that day, I wasn't laughing at all!
